description: A signed statement by the Fendix release pipeline about one engine release: which sources built it, which executables it produced, and which managed-CI contract and finding policy those executables implement. The backend imports a verified record administratively and then accepts managed evidence only from an executable it names. The record states facts about a build; it never states a security decision.

artifacts.description: One entry per published executable. Executable digests differ per OS and architecture, so a release has several — and each is pinned separately, because an allowlist keyed by version alone would accept any of them, including one never published.

download_name.description: Name of the published release asset this executable was distributed as. Identity for humans and for the installer; it is never what the backend matches on.

executable_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the EXECUTABLE ITSELF, uncompressed and unwrapped. Never an archive checksum, a container manifest digest or a source hash: managed evidence carries the digest of the running binary, and only the same kind of digest can match it.

os.description: Target operating system of this executable.

contract.description: The managed-CI contract these executables were built against.

bundle_sha256.description: Digest of the canonical contract bundle as built, so a record cannot claim a revision whose contents differ from what was used.

finding_policy_version.description: The finding policy the engine implements and whose vectors it reproduces.

name.description: Contract these executables produce evidence for.

revision.description: Canonical repository commit the bundle was taken from.

created_at.description: When the release pipeline produced this record (UTC, RFC 3339).

engine_version.description: The released engine version, exactly as the executable reports it.

commit.description: Exact commit the release was built from.

tag.description: Release tag the pipeline ran for.

workflow.description: The release workflow identity that must also appear in the signature's certificate. The signature proves who signed; this states who the signer must be, so the two can be compared rather than trusted separately.

issuer.description: OIDC issuer expected in the signing certificate.

ref.description: Git ref the workflow ran on, normally the release tag ref.

run_id.description: The workflow run that produced the artifacts.

title: Signed engine build record
